A $75M Series C-1 (2024, ~$575M post) appears only in Sacra/tracker data and is excluded. Sum of sourced rounds $284M (includes 2025 rounds whose instrument type may not be pure equity). Private.
notable_investors: EIFO (Export and Investment Fund of Denmark) (lead)

companies.name: Twelve
companies.description: The carbon transformation company.
companies.funding_notes: Twelve (twelve.co; formerly Opus 12), Berkeley, CA; electrochemical CO2-to-fuels/chemicals ('the carbon transformation company'), building AirPlant One e-SAF plant in Moses Lake, WA. Series A $57M (Jul 2021), Series B $130M (Jun 2022, DCVC), Series C $200M (Sep 2024, TPG/Capricorn/Pulse Fund) as part of a $645M package that also included $400M project-level equity led by TPG Rise Climate and $45M loans (both excluded from corporate equity total). ~$11M seed (2019) appears only on trackers, excluded. Earlier government research grants as Opus 12 not itemized. Sum of corporate rounds $387M. Private.

companies.name: Watershed
companies.description: Leading companies use Watershed , the enterprise climate platform, to measure, report, and act on their emissions. Analyze your carbon footprint across your whole business––down to each product and supplier––make real reductions and report out to stakeholders.
companies.funding_notes: Watershed (watershed.com), San Francisco; enterprise climate/carbon accounting platform. Series A at Feb 2021 launch co-led by Sequoia and Kleiner Perkins (amount undisclosed by company; ~$14M per trackers), Series B $70M (Feb 2022, Sequoia + Kleiner, $1B valuation), Series C $100M (Feb 2024, Greenoaks, $1.8B valuation). amount_raised sums B+C ($170M); ~$184M including tracker-reported Series A. Private.

companies.name: Weavegrid
companies.description: WeaveGrid is a software platform that brings together utilities, automakers, and charging companies to predict and manage the unique challenges created by the accelerating adoption of electric vehicles.
companies.funding_notes: WeaveGrid (weavegrid.com), San Francisco; EV charging grid-management software connecting utilities, automakers and chargers. Series A $15M (May 2021, Coatue lead with BEV), Series B $35M (Nov 2022, Salesforce Ventures lead; Emerson Collective new investor). Seed not sourced. Total $50M from sourced rounds. Private.

companies.name: X-energy
companies.description: Advanced Nuclear Energy to Empower Earth.
companies.funding_notes: X-energy (x-energy.com), Rockville, MD; Xe-100 high-temperature gas-cooled SMRs and TRISO-X fuel. Planned SPAC with Ares Acquisition Corp terminated Oct 2023; Series C finalized at $235M (Dec 2023, incl. $80M added by founder Kam Ghaffarian and Ares). Series C-1 announced ~$500M Oct 2024 anchored by Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund, upsized/closed at $700M (Feb 2025). Series D $700M (Nov 2025, Jane Street lead). IPO on Nasdaq (XE) priced Apr 23, 2026 at $23/share, 44.25M shares (~$1.02B gross), closed Apr 27, 2026. amount_raised = sum of sourced private rounds C, C-1, D ($1.635B); earlier founder-funded/Series A-B rounds not itemized, and the IPO proceeds plus large DOE ARDP cost-share awards are excluded. Investor lists for C-1 and D beyond named leads not itemized.

companies.name: Xcimer Energy
companies.description: Xcimer Energy combines novel laser technology with proven science to commercialize laser fusion energy. Its mission is to develop a source of unlimited, clean, safe and reliable energy.

grants.name: DOE Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program award (selected 2023)

companies.funding_notes: xcimer.energy; founded 2022, HQ Denver, CO (office in Redwood City, CA); laser-driven inertial fusion. $100M Series A (June 2024) led by Hedosophia with Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Lowercarbon, Prelude, Emerson Collective, Gigascale, Starlight. Selected for a $9M DOE Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program award in 2023 (grant, excluded from equity total). Small 2022 seed amounts (~$0.9M + ~$0.4M, reportedly led by Wireframe Ventures) appear only on tracker sites, not in primary sources, so they are not listed.

companies.name: Zap Energy
companies.description: Unique fusion systems that don’t rely on magnets or lasers, offering the potential for a new carbon-free energy source with less scale, complexity and cost than competing technologies.
companies.funding_notes: zapenergy.com; founded 2017 (University of Washington spinout), HQ Everett/Seattle, WA; sheared-flow-stabilized Z-pinch fusion. Series B $27.5M (May 2021, led by Addition), Series C $160M (June 2022, led by Lowercarbon), Series D $130M (Sept/Oct 2024, led by Soros Fund Management; Emerson Collective new investor). amount_raised sums the three sourced rounds; the company says total funding surpasses $330M (earlier seed/Series A and ARPA-E/DOE awards not itemized here). Participates in DOE Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program (award amount not captured).

companies.name: Affirm
companies.description: Payment network that empowers consumers and helps merchants drive growth.
companies.funding_notes: affirm.com; HQ San Francisco; founded 2012 by Max Levchin (HVF). Public on Nasdaq (AFRM) since its Jan 2021 IPO (28.29M shares at $49, ~$1.31B gross incl. over-allotment per SEC 8-K). Sourced private rounds: 2015 $275M equity+debt (split not disclosed, Spark Capital Growth lead), Series D $100M (2016, Founders Fund), Series F $300M (2019, Thrive), Series G $500M (2020, GIC & Durable). amount_raised sums only the sourced, equity-only D/F/G rounds; seed-Series C, the 2015 equity portion and the ~2017 Series E are not itemized, so the list is not exhaustive. IPO proceeds excluded from the total.

companies.name: Chime
companies.description: Financial technology company founded on the premise that basic banking services should be helpful, easy and affordable. So that members - everyday people - achieve financial peace of mind.
companies.funding_notes: chime.com; HQ San Francisco; consumer fintech (banking via partner banks). Private rounds: Series C $70M (2018, Menlo), D $200M (Mar 2019, DST; $1.5B), E $500M (Dec 2019, DST; $5.8B), F $485M (Sept 2020; $14.5B), G $750M (Aug 2021, Sequoia Global Equities; $25B). IPO on Nasdaq (CHYM) June 12, 2025 raising ~$864M (includes selling-shareholder shares; excluded from total). Seed-Series B not itemized; amount_raised sums sourced C-G only.

companies.name: Coinbase
companies.description: Aims to increase economic freedom by offering a trusted platform for crypto trading, staking, and transfers, while supporting onchain activity.

Private rounds: Series A $5M (2013, USV), B $25M (2013, a16z), C $75M (2015, DFJ Growth), D $100M (2017, IVP; $1.6B), E $300M (2018, Tiger Global; $8B). Seed/YC money not itemized. Went public via Nasdaq direct listing (COIN) April 14, 2021 (no primary capital raised). List covers the major priced rounds and may not be exhaustive.

companies.name: Divvy
companies.description: Rent-to-own platform enabling access to home ownership and financial stability.
companies.funding_notes: Divvy Homes (divvyhomes.com) - the rent-to-own company matching the description (not Divvy spend management/Bill.com). Founded 2017, San Francisco; incubated at Max Levchin's HVF. Series B $43M (Sept 2019), Series C $110M (Feb 2021, Tiger Global), Series D $200M (Aug 2021, Tiger Global & Caffeinated, ~$2B valuation). Earlier seed/Series A not itemized; amount_raised sums sourced B-D equity only (excludes debt facilities). Acquired by Brookfield (Maymont Homes) in Jan 2025 for ~ $1B.

companies.name: Pilot
companies.description: Finance, accounting, and tax services for startups and growing businesses.
companies.funding_notes: pilot.com (startup bookkeeping/tax/CFO services), HQ San Francisco. Series B $40M (Apr 2019, Index Ventures), Series C $60M (Jan 2021, Sequoia; company said total funding then $120M), Series C expanded to $100M (Mar 2021, Bezos Expeditions & Whale Rock; $1.2B valuation). Pre-Series B funding (~$20M implied) not itemized; amount_raised = company-stated $120M total after Jan 2021 Series C + $40M March 2021 extension = ~$160M.

companies.name: Ramp
companies.description: Financial Operations platform designed to save businesses time and money
companies.funding_notes: ramp.com; HQ New York; corporate cards/spend management. Major rounds: $25M (Feb 2020, Founders Fund), Series B $115M (Apr 2021, D1 & Stripe; $1.6B), Series C $300M (Aug 2021, Founders Fund; $3.9B), Mar 2022 $200M equity (part of $750M incl. $550M debt; $8.1B), Series D $300M (Aug 2023; $5.8B), D-2 $150M (Apr 2024; $7.65B), Series E $200M (Jun 2025; $16B), E-2 $500M (Jul 2025, ICONIQ; $22.5B), $300M (Nov 2025, Lightspeed; $32B), $750M (Jun 2026, ICONIQ/GIC/OTPP; $44B). Ramp said total equity was $2.3B as of Nov 2025 and 'more than $3B' after June 2026; amount_raised = $2.3B + $750M. A late-2020 ~$30M Series A3 (D1/Coatue) is not itemized. Bloomberg reported (Oct 2026, unconfirmed by Ramp) a further ~$1.85B round at ~$60B pre-money led by Dragoneer and Thrive; excluded from rounds/total until confirmed.

companies.name: Stripe
companies.description: Building economic infrastructure for the internet.

investors: Goldman Sachs Asset and Wealth Management

companies.funding_notes: stripe.com; dual HQ San Francisco & Dublin; private. companies.name: Airbnb
companies.description: A global platform connecting travelers with unique places to stay.
companies.round: IPO (Series F last private equity round)
companies.funding_notes: airbnb.com; HQ San Francisco; founded 2008 (YC W09; ~$600K Sequoia seed 2009). Rounds: Series A $7.2M (Nov 2010, Sequoia & Greylock), Series B $112M (Jul 2011, a16z), Series D ~$450M (2014, TPG; reported $450M-$500M, $10B valuation), Series E $1.5B (2015, $25.5B), Series F ~$1.003B closed Mar 2017 at $31B (CapitalG & TCV). Apr 2020: $1B from Silver Lake & Sixth Street in mixed debt + equity (equity split not disclosed; excluded). IPO on Nasdaq (ABNB) Dec 10, 2020 at $68/share, ~$3.7B gross (excluded from total). Series C (~2012) and seed not itemized; list may not be exhaustive. amount_raised sums the five listed equity rounds.

companies.name: Gusto
companies.description: Gusto is a people platform that enables businesses to hire, onboard, pay, insure and support their teams. Gusto Embedded enables software developers to offer in-app modern payroll services to their customers.
companies.funding_notes: gusto.com (formerly ZenPayroll); YC-backed; HQ San Francisco. Series C $140M (Jul 2018, T. Rowe Price, YC Continuity, General Catalyst; ~$2B+), Series D $200M (Jul 2019, Fidelity & Generation; $3.8B), Series E $175M (Aug 2021, T. Rowe Price; $9.5B; Emerson Collective participated), Series E extension May 2022 (undisclosed, reportedly ~ $55M per TechCrunch via Finovate). amount_raised = ~$746M total reported by Finovate (citing TechCrunch reporting) around the extension - approximate. Seed/Series A not itemized; still private. A 2015 ~$50M Series B (CapitalG, General Catalyst) is reported but not verified from a primary source, so it is not itemized.

companies.name: Handshake
companies.description: The best place to launch a career with no connections, experience, or luck required.

Series C $40M (Oct 2018, EQT Ventures; $275M), Series D $80M (Oct 2020, GGV), Series E $80M (May 2021, >$1.5B valuation), Series F $200M (Jan 2022, Coatue & Valiant Peregrine; $3.5B; Emerson Collective participated). amount_raised sums sourced C-F only; seed/Series A/B (Lightspeed, True Ventures, Spark) not itemized. No newer priced round found as of Oct 2026. Series E lead attribution (Lightspeed/Spark) from search summary, not verified on the release.

companies.name: Homebase

Series B $20M (Jun 2018, Bain Capital Ventures), Series C $71M (Jul 2021, GGV), Series D $60M (Apr 2024, L Catterton Growth with Emerson Collective). Seed/Series A not itemized; amount_raised sums sourced B-D only.

companies.name: Syndio

Company stated total funding of $83M after the Series C (earlier seed/Series A not itemized). No later round found; still independent (acquired Embrace.ai in 2026).

companies.name: Anonymous Content

Sept 2016: Emerson Collective took a substantial minority stake with board representation; amount, stake size and valuation not disclosed (reports said the company had sought ~$100M for a 49% stake, with the Emerson valuation reportedly higher - not a confirmed figure). Not a priced venture round. Later expanded via JVs/acquisitions (Endeavor Content TV JV 2022, Automatik, etc.); no further disclosed equity raise found.

companies.name: The Athletic
companies.description: Subscription-based media publisher of smarter sports coverage for die-hard fans.
companies.funding_notes: theathletic.com (now nytimes.com/athletic); founded 2016 in San Francisco (YC-backed). Series B $20M (Mar 2018, Evolution Media), Series C $40M (Oct 2018, Founders Fund & Bedrock), Series D $50M (Jan 2020, Bedrock; ~ $500M valuation; Emerson Collective participated). Axios reported $139.5M total raised since 2016 (used as amount_raised; seed/Series A not itemized). Acquired by The New York Times Company for $550M cash (announced Jan 6, 2022; closed Q1 2022).

companies.name: The Atlantic
companies.description: For more than 150 years, The Atlantic has shaped the national conversation.
companies.funding_notes: theatlantic.com; 1857-founded magazine, HQ Washington, DC. Not a venture-backed startup: in July 2017 Emerson Collective agreed to acquire a majority stake from David G. Bradley (Atlantic Media), terms undisclosed; Bradley kept a minority stake and stayed chairman, with Emerson holding an option to buy the rest. No priced equity round; deal value not public.

companies.name: Axios
companies.description: News media company delivering vital, trustworthy news and analysis in a sharable, “smart brevity” format.
companies.funding_notes: axios.com; HQ Arlington, VA; founded 2016 by Jim VandeHei, Mike Allen and Roy Schwartz. $10M Series A (Sept 2016, Lerer Hippeau; Emerson Collective participated), $20M (Nov 2017, Greycroft & Lerer Hippeau), Series C in Dec 2019 led by Glade Brook (Vox/Recode reported '$20M or more'; the ~$27M figure appears only on tracker sites, so amount left null and excluded). amount_raised = sourced $30M (true total likely ~ $57M). Cox Enterprises acquired majority control in Aug 2022 at a $525M valuation (cash).

companies.name: Hello Sunshine
companies.description: Founded by Reese Witherspoon, Hello Sunshine is a media company that puts women at the center of every story we create, celebrate and discover.
companies.funding_notes: hello-sunshine.com; Los Angeles media company founded 2016 by Reese Witherspoon. Otter Media (AT&T/WarnerMedia) already held a stake, and in Feb 2019 Emerson Collective invested while Otter increased its stake - amounts and round type not disclosed. Aug 2021: majority stake acquired by Candle Media (Kevin Mayer/Tom Staggs, backed by Blackstone) in a deal valuing it at ~ $900M, buying out Otter Media and Emerson Collective.

companies.name: Pushkin Industries
companies.description: Award-winning audio company founded by Malcolm Gladwell and Jacob Weisberg; Revisionist History , Broken Record , The Happiness Lab and more.
companies.funding_notes: pushkin.fm; New York-based audio/podcast company co-founded 2018 by Malcolm Gladwell and Jacob Weisberg. EDGAR shows Form D filings (CIK 1756861) dated 2019-02-04 and 2021-03-24; tracker sites put these at ~$2.3M (2019 'seed', Emerson Collective listed as investor) and ~$10.5M (Mar 2021) but I could not open the Form D documents (SEC site under maintenance) to confirm amounts or security type, so amounts are left null and no priced round type is public. Acquired Transmitter Media in July 2022. Still independent as of Oct 2026 per available sources.

companies.name: Within/Supernatural
companies.description: Launched in 2020, Supernatural is an immersive, virtual reality fitness experience that combines the best music, coaches, destinations and movements into an incredible home workout.
companies.funding_notes: Within Unlimited (within.com / getsupernatural.com), Los Angeles VR studio (formerly Vrse) founded by Chris Milk and Aaron Koblin; launched Supernatural VR fitness in 2020. Series A ~$12.6M (Jun 2016, a16z; reported $12.5M-$12.6M), Series B $40M (Jul 2017, Temasek & Emerson Collective). Acquired by Meta, closing Feb 2023 after the FTC lost its injunction bid; price undisclosed (The Information reported ~ $400M). Any later pre-acquisition rounds not found.
